message.content: Trade shaped the pharaoh’s powers. It gave him resources, and their caravans brought wealth. His officials controlled those routes, and they collected taxes. We can see that his authority grew, and her role in temple economies rose. Their imports helped him project power, and you can trace their influence in his records. My view is that such exchange made him more dependent on his agents and less self-sufficient. I think he benefited, and she supported him. They protected his goods, and her temples stored their tribute. The king rewarded his loyalists, and their allies gained influence. We should note that their partners saw him as a reliable buyer. His power depended on their cooperation, and he needed their routes. Your question highlights how exchange shaped his reach; my answer is that it expanded his political and economic power.
